rationale: Starting from scratch, I designed a balanced robot geometry with 5 sensors spaced evenly across the front to detect the line effectively. I chose a medium sensor size (0.012 m) to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track and body width are set to 0.14 m to provide stability without excessive width that could cause off-track penalties. The wheel radius is 0.035 m for a good balance of speed and torque, and the mass is set to 0.8 kg for moderate inertia. The controller uses a base speed of 1.5 to aim for a fast pace while maintaining control. PID gains are set to moderate values (kp=8, ki=0.5, kd=3) to provide responsive but stable steering. Sensor weights are arranged to steer left when the line is detected on the left sensors and right when on the right sensors, with the center sensor having a strong positive weight to keep the robot centered. The line loss strategy is 'last_direction' to continue turning in the last known direction to recover the line. I request a broad set of observations including completion, progress, errors, line loss events, and control effort to analyze performance and guide future improvements.
